items.plain: Just as a plant grows by itself while you only protect it, spiritual growth comes from within. Nobody can make you spiritual; you must teach yourself.
items.core_idea: Spiritual growth comes from inside; no one can impose it.

items.plain: The ideal person has philosophy, mysticism, feeling and work all fully present. Most people are one-sided and fear other paths; being balanced in all four is the ideal of religion.
items.core_idea: True religion balances thought, mysticism, feeling and work.

items.plain: Inspiration grows out of reason, so it completes reason rather than opposing it, just as an old man completes rather than contradicts the child he was.
items.core_idea: Inspiration fulfils reason instead of contradicting it.

items.plain: Whatever you do, from blacking shoes to worshipping God, concentration makes you do it better. Concentration is the one key that opens nature and the treasure-house of knowledge.
items.core_idea: Concentration is the key to all knowledge and skill.

items.plain: Our minds are scattered over a hundred things. The moment I try to calm my thoughts and focus on one thing, thousands of unwanted impulses and thoughts rush in and disturb me.
items.core_idea: The mind scatters the moment we try to focus.

items.plain: All misery comes from attachment: we help people, they turn ungrateful, and we suffer. Karma-Yoga teaches working for its own sake, giving without wanting anything back, and so escaping misery.
items.core_idea: Work without attachment, give without expecting return.

items.plain: Wherever there is love, the Lord is there: in a husband's kiss, a mother's kiss, friends clasping hands, a great person helping humanity. Wherever the heart opens, God shows himself.
items.core_idea: God is present wherever there is love.

items.plain: A lower bird, happy and miserable by turns among sweet and bitter fruits, keeps nearing a calm golden bird above until it finds it was that bird all along. The upper bird is God; the lower, the soul.
items.core_idea: The suffering self is really the calm divine Self.
items.extended_text: Upon the same tree there are two birds, one on the top, the other below. The one on the top is calm, silent, and majestic, immersed in his own glory; the one on the lower branches, eating sweet and bitter fruits by turns, hopping from branch to branch, is becoming happy and miserable by turns. After a time the lower bird eats an exceptionally bitter fruit and gets disgustful and looks up and sees the other bird, that wondrous one of golden plumage, who eats neither sweet nor bitter fruit, who is neither happy nor miserable, but calm, Selfcentred, and sees nothing beyond his Self. The lower bird longs for this condition but soon forgets it, and again begins to eat the fruits. In a little while, he eats another exceptionally bitter fruit, which makes him feel miserable, and he again looks up, and tries to get nearer to the upper bird. Once more he forgets and after a time he looks up, and so on he goes again and again, until he comes very near to the beautiful bird and sees the reflection of light from his plumage playing around his own body, and he feels a change and seems to melt away; still nearer he comes, and everything about him melts away, and at last he understands this wonderful change. The lower bird was, as it were, only the substantial-looking shadow, the reflection of the higher; he himself was in essence the upper bird all the time. This eating of fruits, sweet and bitter, this lower, little bird, weeping and happy by turns, was a vain chimera, a dream: all along, the real bird was there above, calm and silent, glorious and majestic, beyond grief, beyond sorrow. The upper bird is God, the Lord of this universe; and the lower bird is the human soul, eating the sweet and bitter fruits of this world.

items.plain: We can agree with foolish ideas today and drop them tomorrow, but true religion does not change. Religion is realisation: not talk or theory, but your whole soul becoming what it believes.
items.core_idea: Religion is realisation and becoming, not doctrine.

items.plain: In action we are so powerless; our will is blocked at every turn. We can want anything, even to reach a distant star, yet the body lets us achieve very few of our desires.
items.core_idea: Our desires are boundless but our power is small.

items.plain: Small things hurt us because we think we are small, finite beings. Though it is hard, amid misery I must believe I am infinite; and we really are, always seeking something infinite and free.
items.core_idea: Misery comes from believing we are finite.

items.plain: Even in the deepest misery the Soul sends a ray of light, and we wake to find we can never lose what is truly ours. Our existence comes first, before good or bad; it is never lost.
items.core_idea: Our true existence can never be lost.

items.plain: No one can die or be degraded forever; life is a playground, however rough the game. However hard the blows, the Soul is never harmed, for we are that Infinite.
items.core_idea: The Soul is never injured by life's blows.

items.plain: Often near death from hunger and exhaustion, collapsing under a tree, his mind turned to the thought that he was It, beyond fear, death and hunger, and nature could not crush him. Then he would rise renewed.
items.core_idea: Asserting the inner Self gives strength in extremity.

items.plain: Do not be afraid, and do not count how many times you fail, for time is endless. Keep going, assert yourself again and again, and light will come.
items.core_idea: Keep going despite failures; light will come.

items.plain: Only you can lift yourself up; you are your own worst enemy and best friend. So hold on to the Self, stand up, do not fear, and let the Self emerge amid all weakness, however faint at first.
items.core_idea: You alone are your enemy and your friend.

items.plain: I am like the unchanging blue sky with clouds passing over it. Happiness and misery, good and evil, may hide the Self for a moment, but they are finite and pass, while I remain.
items.core_idea: Joys and sorrows pass; the Self stays unchanged.

items.plain: Do not be afraid, and do not believe that we are evil, limited, or that we can ever die. None of that is true.
items.core_idea: We are not evil, finite or mortal.

fix.display_text: Fear not. Believe not that we are evil, that we are finite, that we can ever die. It is not true.
fix.reason: Removed stray full stop after comma.

items.plain: There are two paths, enjoyment and blessedness, and both pull at people. Whoever chooses blessedness becomes wise; whoever chooses enjoyment declines.
items.core_idea: Choosing blessedness over enjoyment makes a sage.

items.plain: The Self you ask about is never born and never dies, and it is not destroyed when the body is. Neither killer nor killed is right, since the Self cannot kill or be killed.
items.core_idea: The Self is unborn, undying and cannot be killed.

items.plain: The body is a chariot, the senses horses, the mind the reins, the intellect the driver and the soul the rider. Without control and discernment the senses run wild; with them they are like well-trained horses.
items.core_idea: A controlled mind keeps the senses in check.

items.plain: Wake up and act. Do not stop until you reach the goal, for the sages say the path is as hard as walking a razor's edge.
items.core_idea: Persist to the goal though the path is hard.

items.plain: As street noise drowns out the person beside you, the world's noise pulls the mind outward. To see the Self, that outward pull must stop; turn your eyes inward and you will see the Lord's glory within.
items.core_idea: Turn inward from the world's noise to see the Self.

items.plain: When every desire troubling the heart ends, the mortal becomes immortal and reaches Brahman here. Only when the heart's crookedness goes and its knots are cut does one become immortal.
items.core_idea: Freedom from desire makes the mortal immortal.

items.plain: People hurt each other out of fear of not having enough. A man afraid he will lack money is driven by that fear to harm and rob others.
items.core_idea: Fear of scarcity drives people to harm others.

items.plain: I should love everyone, my brother included, because we are one. The whole universe is bound together in that oneness.
items.core_idea: Love everyone because all are one.

items.plain: When Yajnavalkya offered his wife all his wealth before leaving, she asked whether a world full of riches could make her immortal. He said no: wealth makes you rich, nothing more.
items.core_idea: Wealth cannot give immortality.

items.plain: Look at our own lives: as children we think bad things good and good things bad. Our ideas keep changing and rising; what once seemed very good no longer seems so.
items.core_idea: Our ideas of good and evil change as we grow.

items.plain: Our hatred of others comes from foolish ideas of good and evil absorbed since childhood. They distort our judgment and turn the earth into hell; give them up and it becomes heaven.
items.core_idea: Ideas of good and evil breed hatred.

items.plain: Rain rises from the ocean and flows back to it; trees end in seeds that become trees; birds leave eggs. Everything starts from fine seeds, grows grosser, and returns to that fine form.
items.core_idea: All things arise from seeds and return to them.

fix.display_text: The raindrop is drawn from the ocean in the form of vapour, and drifts away through the air to the mountains; there it changes again into water and flows back through hundreds of miles down to the mother ocean. The seed produces the tree. The tree dies, leaving only the seed. Again it comes up as another tree, which again ends in the seed, and so on. Look at a bird, how from the egg it springs, becomes a beautiful bird, lives its life and then dies, leaving only other eggs, containing germs of future birds. So with the animals; so with men. Everything begins, as it were, from certain seeds, certain rudiments, certain fine forms, and becomes grosser and grosser as it develops; and then again it goes back to that fine form and subsides.

items.plain: Man watches all these changes and is never impure himself; he only seems so by reflection, as a clear crystal looks red or blue beside a coloured flower while staying pure.
items.core_idea: The self only appears impure, like coloured crystal.

items.plain: Nature is always changing but the soul never changes, and because nature changes, the soul can come out of its bondage.
items.core_idea: Changing nature lets the unchanging soul become free.

items.plain: Someone who calls himself a sinner says something untrue, because he does not know himself. He is deeply ignorant, knowing only a small part of what he is.
items.core_idea: Calling yourself a sinner shows self-ignorance.

items.plain: The soul feels neither pleasure nor pain; it is the eternal witness of all action and takes no fruit from it. Like the sun or a crystal, it is untouched, beyond both passive and active.
items.core_idea: The soul is the untouched witness of all action.

items.plain: Every person exists, every person must know, and every person is mad for love and cannot help loving. All beings, lowest to highest, must love.
items.core_idea: Every being exists, knows and loves.

items.plain: The soul's true nature is unlimited bliss, but whatever shows itself is limited. So love as we know it shifts: I love you one day, hate you the next, because it is only a manifestation.
items.core_idea: Expressed love is limited; the soul's bliss is not.

items.plain: If you think you are bound, you stay bound, making your own chains; if you know you are free, you are free right now. Freedom is the goal of all nature.
items.core_idea: Believing yourself bound keeps you bound.

items.plain: Cut yourself off and everything hurts you; reach out and feel for others and you are helped. The selfish man is the most miserable; the happiest has no selfishness at all.
items.core_idea: Selfishness brings misery; caring for others brings help.

items.plain: Which version of me is my real individuality: the baby sucking its thumb? In fifty years I will laugh at who I am now, as I now laugh at that baby.
items.core_idea: Our individuality keeps changing; which one is real?

items.plain: If your pleasure depends on something outside you, you suffer when it goes; nothing in the universe is reliable. If all my joy is in myself, I always have it, because I can never lose my Self.
items.core_idea: Joy found in the Self cannot be lost.

items.plain: We make mistakes, so what; it is all play, so do not weep and repent over past sins. Keep going and do not look back, for there is nothing to gain from it.
items.core_idea: Don't dwell on past mistakes; keep moving forward.

items.plain: Know for certain that you are in everything. That is why you should hurt no one: hurting them, you hurt yourself.
items.core_idea: Hurting others is hurting yourself.

items.plain: Whoever sees the One amid the many, the one life amid endless death, and the changeless within their own soul, to that person belongs eternal peace.
items.core_idea: Seeing the changeless One brings eternal peace.

items.plain: Evil is an iron chain and good a golden one, but both bind. Use the golden chain to loosen the iron one, as you use one thorn to remove another, then throw both away and be free.
items.core_idea: Good and evil both bind; go beyond both.

items.plain: Always be the giver: give love, help, service, any little thing, with no bargaining, no conditions and nothing expected back. Give freely from your own abundance, as God gives to us.
items.core_idea: Give freely and expect nothing in return.

items.plain: In our struggles the world seems dreadful, but as we watch puppies nip each other in play without worry, our struggles are only play to God. The world amuses God, and nothing in it angers God.
items.core_idea: Our struggles are only play in God's eyes.

items.plain: A cry to the divine Mother: my boat is sinking in life's sea, illusion and attachment are raging, my senses are foolish and my mind weak, and I am lost. Mother, save me!
items.core_idea: A desperate plea to the Mother to be saved.

items.plain: Be brave and sincere, follow any path with devotion, and you will reach the Whole. Grasp one link and the whole chain follows; water the roots, reach the Lord, and you have everything.
items.core_idea: Sincere devotion on any path leads to God.

items.plain: His Master called the world a madhouse where people chase money, sex or fame and a few chase God, which he preferred. God turns us to gold at once: we look the same but can no longer hurt or sin.
items.core_idea: Better to be mad after God than worldly things.

items.plain: Follow the scriptures until you can go beyond them, since books are not the goal and each person must verify religious truth. Trust only the teacher who says you can see it too.
items.core_idea: Verify religious truth yourself; books aren't the end.

items.plain: There are three kinds of love: one takes and gives nothing, one is a trade, and one gives with no thought of return, like a moth drawn to a flame.
items.core_idea: The highest love seeks nothing in return.

items.plain: Misery always follows happiness, and both are chains that hide our true nature. Behind them is the Atman, whose nature is unchanging bliss and peace; we already have it and need only wash away the dross.
items.core_idea: Beyond happiness and misery lies the Self's bliss.

items.plain: A mind pleased by praise will be hurt by blame. Pleasures of the senses and mind are fleeting, but within us is one true joy that depends on nothing; it is free, it is bliss.
items.core_idea: True joy lies within, independent of praise.

items.plain: Neither chase nor avoid; accept what comes, for freedom is being unaffected, not merely enduring. Be like the bull who told an apologetic mosquito to bring its whole family to live on his horn.
items.core_idea: Freedom is being untouched by what comes.

items.plain: We do our best work and have our greatest influence when we are not thinking of ourselves. All great geniuses know this.
items.core_idea: Our best work comes without thought of self.

items.plain: Our thoughts have made us what we are, so be careful what you think. Words matter less; thoughts live on and travel far.
items.core_idea: We become what we think.

items.plain: Bless people when they insult you. Think how much good they do you; they can only harm themselves.
items.core_idea: Bless those who insult you.

items.plain: We give things up and press on, find nothing and fall into despair; but hold on, keep holding on.
items.core_idea: Hold on through the despair of renunciation.

items.plain: Be like a lily: stay where you are and open your petals, and the bees will come on their own.
items.core_idea: Unfold where you are and others will come.

items.plain: Seek truth only for its own sake, not for bliss, which may come but must not be your motive; have no motive except God. Dare to reach Truth even if it means going through hell.
items.core_idea: Seek truth for its own sake.

items.plain: The whole universe is the one Self with variations, like one tune made bearable by variety. Its discords only make the harmony that follows more perfect.
items.core_idea: The universe is one Self in many variations.

items.plain: Every thought is a small hammer blow on the iron of our bodies, shaping them into what we want them to be.
items.core_idea: Each thought shapes who we become.

items.plain: The source of all knowledge is in everyone, ant or angel, and true religion is one; we only quarrel over forms and symbols. Paradise exists for those who find it; we lose ourselves and think the world is lost.
items.core_idea: All knowledge is within; true religion is one.

items.plain: The divine light in most people is hidden like a lamp in an iron cask, but purity and unselfishness thin the cask until it is clear as glass, as in Ramakrishna. The impatient never succeed.
items.core_idea: Purity makes the hidden inner light visible.

items.plain: Forcing reform only slows it. Do not tell someone they are bad; tell them they are good but can be better.
items.core_idea: Encourage people to be better; don't condemn.

items.plain: Love never condemns; only ambition does. There is no such thing as righteous anger or justified killing.
items.core_idea: Love never condemns; no anger is righteous.

items.plain: The more love and goodness grow in us, the more we see them around us, and condemning others condemns ourselves. Set your own small world right and the larger world will follow.
items.core_idea: Change yourself and the world changes with you.

items.plain: Every real step forward in the world has been won by love. Criticism has been tried for thousands of years and never helps; condemnation achieves nothing.
items.core_idea: Love achieves progress; condemnation achieves nothing.

items.plain: Never ask what good something will do for the world; leave the world alone. Love and ask nothing, look for nothing more, and forget all the isms.
items.core_idea: Love without asking for results.

items.plain: A Sufi poem: once there were a woman and a man, but love grew until there was neither, only a faint memory of two, because love came between them and made them one.
items.core_idea: Love dissolves two into one.

items.plain: All hatred is the self killing the Self, so love is the law of life.
items.core_idea: Hatred harms the Self; love is life's law.

items.plain: Striking back is easy. It is enormously hard to hold back, stand still, take refuge in the Lord, and wait for Him to act.
items.core_idea: Restraint and surrender are harder than striking.

items.plain: You cannot see the truth unless you are ready to change at any moment, yet you must stay firm and steady in your search for it.
items.core_idea: Stay open to change yet steady in seeking truth.

items.plain: The universe is ours to enjoy, but want nothing. Wanting is weakness; it makes us beggars, and we are children of the king, not beggars.
items.core_idea: Wanting makes beggars of royal children.

items.plain: Religion without philosophy turns into superstition; philosophy without religion turns into dry atheism.
items.core_idea: Religion and philosophy need each other.

items.plain: Seeing difference causes all misery, and ignorance causes us to see difference.
items.core_idea: Ignorance makes us see difference, causing misery.

items.plain: We are lamps, and our burning is what we call life; when the oxygen runs out, the lamp goes out. All we can do is keep the lamp clean.
items.core_idea: Life burns out; we can only keep it clean.

items.plain: His Master said the vulture flies high out of sight, yet its eye is always on some scrap of carrion on the ground.
items.core_idea: Soaring high means little if your eye is low.

items.plain: Knowledge kept in books and money held by others are as good as having no knowledge and no money.
items.core_idea: Knowledge and money must truly be your own.

items.plain: Devotion is natural and pleasant; philosophy turns the stream back to its source, faster but very hard. Devotion asks for total self-surrender: a longer way, but easier and happier, where all I do is God doing it.
items.core_idea: Devotion is the easier, happier path to God.

fix.display_text: The path of devotion is natural and pleasant. Philosophy is taking the mountain stream back to its force. It is a quicker method but very hard. Philosophy says, “Check everything.” Devotion says, “Give the stream, have eternal self-surrender.” It is a longer way, but easier and happier. “Thine am I for ever; henceforth whatever I do, it is Thou doing it. No more is there any me or mine.”

items.plain: A prayer: with no money to give, no brains for learning and no time for Yoga, I give You myself, sweet One, my body and my mind.
items.core_idea: Having nothing else, I offer myself to God.

items.plain: Nothing can come between the soul and God; even if there is no God, keep hold of love, for it is better to die seeking God than chasing scraps. Choose the highest ideal and give your life to it.
items.core_idea: Give your life to the highest ideal.

items.plain: Knowledge criticises and fusses over everything, but Love trusts that God will show His true nature and accepts everything.
items.core_idea: Love accepts all; knowledge only criticises.

items.plain: A poem: visiting the sick Rabbia, one saint said pure prayer endures God's punishment, another that loving God's will rejoices in it. Rabbia replied that whoever sees the Master's face forgets being punished at all.
items.core_idea: Seeing God, one forgets all suffering.

fix.display_text: Rabbia, sick upon her bed, By two saints was visited — Holy Malik, Hassan wise — Men of mark in Moslem eyes. Hassan said, “Whose prayer is pure Will God’s chastisements endure.” Malik, from a deeper sense Uttered his experience: “He who loves his master’s choice Will in chastisement rejoice.” Rabbia saw some selfish will In their maxims lingering still, And replied “O men of grace, He who sees his Master’s face, Will not in his prayers recall That he is chastised at all!”
fix.reason: Removed stray spaces before apostrophes and exclamation mark.

items.plain: Every new power brings more misery, so kill desire. Fulfilling any desire is like poking a stick into a hornets' nest.
items.core_idea: Fulfilling desire stirs up more misery.

items.plain: Action is pleasant and all misery is reaction, as a child feels pain only when the burn reacts, so be the witness and do not react. Work freely, not from duty; life is an eternal holiday.
items.core_idea: Misery comes from reaction; be the witness.

items.plain: The secret of existence is to have no fear: never fear what will happen to you, and depend on no one. You are free only when you refuse all help, as a full sponge can absorb no more.
items.core_idea: Fearlessness and self-reliance are the secret of life.

items.plain: Even fighting in self-defence is wrong, though better than attacking. There is no righteous indignation, because indignation comes from failing to see that all things are the same.
items.core_idea: No indignation is righteous; all are one.

items.plain: The greatest sin is to think yourself weak; realise you are Brahman, and nothing has power except what you give it. Deny evil, create none, and declare yourself master, for we make our chains and only we can break them.
items.core_idea: Thinking yourself weak is the greatest sin.

items.plain: Buddha bowed to nothing, not scripture, caste, priest or custom, and reasoned fearlessly as far as reason went, with unmatched love for all life. Like Washington, he won a throne only to give it away, seeking nothing for himself.
items.core_idea: Buddha sought truth fearlessly and nothing for himself.

items.plain: Every step taken in the light is mine forever, as a country becomes yours once you see it. Each of us must see for ourselves; teachers can only bring the food, and we must eat it.
items.core_idea: Truth must be seen for yourself.

items.plain: Hold on to reason until you reach something higher; you will know it is higher because it does not clash with reason.
items.core_idea: What is truly higher never clashes with reason.

items.plain: Do not waste energy talking; meditate and gather power in silence, undisturbed by the world's rush. A beggar has nothing to give; only a king can give, and only when he wants nothing.
items.core_idea: Gather spiritual power in silence.

items.plain: Hold your money only as a caretaker of what belongs to God, without attachment. Let go of name, fame and money, which are a terrible bondage, and feel the wonderful air of freedom.
items.core_idea: Hold wealth without attachment; it binds.

items.plain: The whole ocean stands behind every wave. All things are waves, big and small, and each is the whole ocean in essence, though as a wave it is only a part.
items.core_idea: Each wave is the whole ocean in essence.

items.plain: Religion adds nothing new; it only removes obstacles to seeing your Self. These include sickness, doubt, inconstancy and melancholy, though once you know Brahman you can never be melancholy again.
items.core_idea: Religion removes obstacles to seeing the Self.

items.plain: To gain freedom through work, work without desire or looking for results, neither seeking pleasure nor fearing pain; that leads to knowledge and liberation. It is body and mind that work, not I.
items.core_idea: Work without desire leads to freedom.

items.plain: Do everything as an offering to the Lord, in the world but not of it, like a lotus pure above the mud, and love everyone. We see evil outside only because it is in us; the pure cannot see impurity.
items.core_idea: We see outside only what is within us.

items.plain: Do not fight over methods; aim only at realisation and pick the method that suits you best. Eat the mangoes and let others argue about the basket.
items.core_idea: Seek realisation; don't quarrel over methods.

items.plain: One guess against another leads to fights, but speak of what you have actually lived, and no human heart can resist it.
items.core_idea: Lived experience moves hearts; opinions breed fights.

items.plain: Learn to help without pity or thinking there is misery. Learn to treat enemy and friend alike; when you can, and desire is gone, the goal is reached.
items.core_idea: Help without pity; treat friend and enemy alike.

items.plain: Time devours everything, so why paint the butterfly or run like mice on a treadmill? Every desire, good or bad, brings evil, like meat forever out of a dog's reach, so cut off all desire.
items.core_idea: All desire is futile; cut it off.

items.plain: Four travellers reached a high wall: three climbed and leapt over with joy, and the fourth came back to tell of them. The laughter echoing back from great souls who leapt beyond illusion is our sign something lies beyond.
items.core_idea: Great souls' joy shows there is something beyond.

items.plain: Being allowed to give is our privilege, for only by giving do we grow. The poor suffer so that we may be helped; let the giver kneel and give thanks, and the receiver stand and allow it.
items.core_idea: The giver should thank the one who receives.

items.plain: Be grateful to whoever curses you: they show you a mirror of what cursing is and give you a chance to practise restraint. So bless them and be glad; power grows only through exercise.
items.core_idea: Those who curse you help you grow.

items.plain: Draw the scriptures out of your own Self, for you are the greatest book there is. Outside teaching is useless until the teacher within opens the book of the heart.
items.core_idea: The truest teacher and book are within you.

items.plain: Never say doing anything is your duty; say it is your nature. Truth alone wins, so stand on Truth and you have God.
items.core_idea: Act from your nature; stand on Truth.

items.plain: All knowledge depends on a calm mind.
items.core_idea: Knowledge depends on a calm mind.

items.plain: Whether or not you have controlled your mind or have money, you are the ever-pure Atman. Say: no bondage ever touched me; I am the changeless sky, and passing clouds of belief do not touch me.
items.core_idea: You are the ever-pure Self, untouched by anything.

items.plain: Fear nothing, for you are the essence of existence; be at peace and do not upset yourself. You were never bound, never virtuous or sinful, so drop these delusions and be at peace.
items.core_idea: You were never bound; be at peace.

items.plain: Remove the faults in yourself and you will see none outside; a baby sees a robbery and it means nothing. Once you are free and stainless, you see only freedom and purity around you.
items.core_idea: Free yourself of faults and you'll see none.

items.plain: We have three great gifts: a human body, the nearest reflection of God; the desire to be free; and a noble teacher who has crossed beyond delusion. With these three, thank the Lord; you will surely be free.
items.core_idea: Body, longing and a teacher bring freedom.

items.plain: What you only understand intellectually can be overturned by a new argument, but what you realise is yours forever. Talking religion does little good; make it a habit to see God behind everything.
items.core_idea: Realisation lasts; intellectual belief can be overturned.

items.plain: Ingersoll wanted to squeeze the orange of this world dry. He replied he squeezed it better: knowing he cannot die, he is unhurried and fearless, free of ties, loving everyone as God, and so gets ten thousand times more.
items.core_idea: Fearless love of all gets the most from life.

items.plain: Never judge a person by their faults. Their great virtues are their own; their errors are the common weaknesses of humanity and should not count in judging their character.
items.core_idea: Judge people by their virtues, not faults.

items.plain: All our past actions are really good, because they lead us to what we finally become.
items.core_idea: Every past action leads toward who we become.

items.plain: Tell the truth boldly, whether it hurts or not, and never cater to weakness. If the truth is too much for intelligent people and sweeps them away, let them go, the sooner the better.
items.core_idea: Speak truth boldly, never pandering to weakness.

items.plain: Blows wake us up and help break the dream. They show us the world is not enough and make us long for freedom.
items.core_idea: Life's blows awaken longing for freedom.

items.plain: A restless lower bird, tasting bitter fruit, kept climbing nearer a serene golden bird above. At last it reached the top and found there had only ever been one bird, and it had always been that upper bird.
items.core_idea: The restless self is really the serene Self.

items.plain: Be completely without hope, the highest state, for what is there to hope for? Break the bonds of hope, stand on your Self, be at rest and give everything to God, without hypocrisy.
items.core_idea: Freedom from hope is the highest rest.

items.plain: We want everything except God, because the outer world meets our ordinary needs. Only after hard blows, when we are disappointed with everything here, do we feel the need for something higher and seek God.
items.core_idea: Disappointment with the world turns us to God.

items.plain: Only a fool, living beside the Ganga, digs a little well for water; only a fool, arriving at a diamond mine, looks for glass beads.
items.core_idea: Don't settle for trifles beside the infinite.

items.plain: Books point to the inner light, but once it flashes for you, leave them and look within; you hold far more than all books. Never lose faith in yourself, for all power is yours.
items.core_idea: Look within; never lose faith in yourself.

items.plain: Be grateful to books and teachers without being bound to them; love and worship your Guru, but think for yourself rather than obey blindly. Blind belief cannot save you; work out your own salvation.
items.core_idea: Love your teacher but think for yourself.

items.plain: Any good you do, you do to yourself, so treat the receiver as the higher one. Give as a rose gives perfume, naturally and without knowing it is giving.
items.core_idea: Give naturally, as a rose gives perfume.

items.plain: Be friendly and respectful to all and take the best from each, but keep firm in your own way. Higher still is seeing through another's eyes: while weak, keep one path; when strong, sympathise with every view.
items.core_idea: Hold your path, yet learn to see through others' eyes.

fix.display_text: “Take the honey out of all flowers; sit and be friendly with all, pay reverence to all, say to all, ‘Yes, brother, yes, brother’, but keep firm in your own way.” A higher stage is actually to take the position of the other. If I am all, why can I not really and actively sympathise with my brother and see with his eyes? While I am weak, I must stick to one course (Nishthâ), but when I am strong, I can feel with every other and perfectly sympathise with his ideas.
fix.reason: Removed stray space before closing quote.

items.plain: Now we are like stray dogs eating fearfully in a kitchen, waiting to be chased out. Renounce the world, at least in your heart, and you become a king who knows he owns it.
items.core_idea: Renounce the world to truly own it.

items.plain: Spit out your actions, good or bad, and never think of them again; do not repent, brood or recall your good deeds. You cannot undo the effect, so face it, but never repeat the act.
items.core_idea: Let go of past deeds; face effects, don't repeat.

items.plain: Saying food is not eating it, and saying water is not drinking it. Likewise, merely repeating the word God brings no realisation; we must strive and practise.
items.core_idea: Realisation needs practice, not just words.

items.plain: Only the present exists. Even in thought there is no past or future, because to think of them you must make them present.
items.core_idea: Only the present moment exists.

items.plain: Do not wait to rest with a harp by degrees; take the harp and begin now. Why wait for heaven when you can make it here?
items.core_idea: Don't wait for heaven; make it here.

items.plain: This shameful clinging to life as we know it is the root of all evil, of cheating, stealing and making money a god. Value nothing material and cling to nothing, not even life; then there is no fear.
items.core_idea: Clinging to life is the root of evil and fear.

items.plain: All the great religions taught the golden rule in nearly the same words, but only the Hindus gave the reason: you must love others because they are yourself. There is only One.
items.core_idea: Love others because they are yourself.

items.plain: Of all great religious teachers, only Lao-tze, Buddha and Jesus went beyond the golden rule to say: do good to your enemies and love those who hate you.
items.core_idea: The highest teaching is to love your enemies.

items.plain: Have something of your own to say, or you cannot judge what others have said. Drop old superstitions and stay ready for new truths; only fools drink bitter water from their forefathers' well rather than pure water from others'.
items.core_idea: Stay open to new truths over inherited superstition.

items.plain: Come to God any way you can; just come. But on the way, do not push anyone down.
items.core_idea: Reach God any way, without harming others.

items.plain: Control the lake of your own mind, or you cannot understand another's. A true teacher puts all his force into the learner's own leanings; without real sympathy we can never teach well.
items.core_idea: Master your own mind to teach with sympathy.

fix.display_text: Control the “lake” of your own mind, else you cannot understand the lake of another’s mind. The true teacher is one who can throw his whole force into the tendency of the taught. Without real sympathy we can never teach well.

items.plain: Be honest that you see the ideal but cannot reach it yet, rather than pretending to renounce. If a hundred fall, take the flag and carry it on, for God is true whoever fails.
items.core_idea: Be honest about the ideal; carry the flag on.

items.plain: Give up, and know success will follow even if you never see it. Jesus left only twelve fishermen, yet those few overturned the Roman Empire.
items.core_idea: Success follows renunciation, even unseen.

items.plain: The one who struggles is better than the one who never tries.
items.core_idea: Trying beats never attempting.

items.plain: Truth is judged only by truth, not by the good it does; the sun needs no torch to be seen. Even if truth destroys the universe, it is still truth, so stand by it.
items.core_idea: Truth needs no test beyond itself.

items.plain: Like an ox in an oil-mill chasing hay it never reaches, we chase happiness, grind nature's mill, and die to begin again. Religion begins when we see that seeking happiness in matter is nonsense.
items.core_idea: Religion begins when chasing material happiness fails.

items.plain: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God. If every book and prophet were lost, this one sentence alone would save humanity.
items.core_idea: Purity of heart alone could save humanity.

items.plain: An evil person is part of my own body, like a wound or burn. We must nurse him and help him get better until he heals and is happy and healthy again.
items.core_idea: Heal the wrongdoer like a wound in yourself.

items.plain: Cry for help and you will receive it. In the end the one crying and the Helper both vanish, the play is over, and only the Self remains.
items.core_idea: Seeker and Helper dissolve; only the Self remains.

items.plain: Once you have chosen the ideal and the means, you can almost let the ideal go, sure it will come when the means are perfected. Take care of the cause, and the effect will take care of itself.
items.core_idea: Focus on the means; the result will follow.

items.plain: Our greatest sorrow comes when we pour our energy into something that fails, know it hurts us, and still cannot let go. Like the bee that came for honey, our feet stick to the pot.
items.core_idea: We suffer by clinging to what hurts us.

items.plain: Cold, unloving people escape most of life's miseries, but so does a wall, which never loves or hurts and is still only a wall. Better to be attached and caught than to be a wall.
items.core_idea: Better to love and suffer than feel nothing.

items.plain: We are all beggars, wanting a return for whatever we do. We are traders in life, in virtue, in religion, and sadly even in love.
items.core_idea: We even turn love into a trade.

items.plain: We get caught not by what we give but by what we expect: love brings misery only because we want love back. Without wanting there is no misery; desire is the father of all misery.
items.core_idea: Expecting return, not loving, brings misery.

items.plain: Give what you have and want nothing back; it will return a thousandfold, but do not think of that. All of life is giving, and nature will force you to give, so give willingly.
items.core_idea: Life is giving; give willingly, expecting nothing.

items.plain: Even if every attempt fails and we are torn and bleeding, we must keep our heart and assert our divinity. Nature wants us to hit back blow for blow; not hitting back takes a more than divine power.
items.core_idea: Not striking back takes the greatest strength.

items.plain: Every day we resolve to be unattached, remembering how each attachment made us miserable and enslaved, and we vow to master ourselves. Then the same story repeats, and the soul is caught again, like a bird struggling in a net.
items.core_idea: We vow freedom, then get caught again.

items.plain: The difficulties are huge; most of us lose heart, turn pessimist and stop believing in sincerity, love and everything noble. So people who were kind, simple and forgiving when young become lying masks in old age.
items.core_idea: Discouragement can turn the kind into cynics.

items.plain: Every blow you receive needs your half as well as the world's. You cannot control the world, but you can control your own half, and if you truly master yourself, the blow will never come.
items.core_idea: Control your part and the blow cannot land.

items.plain: Since childhood we blame things outside ourselves, calling the world devilish and people selfish, and try to fix others instead of ourselves. But if we are so good, why are we here among them?
items.core_idea: Stop blaming the world; look at yourself.

items.plain: Take care of yourself and stop attending to others for a while; perfect the means and the end will follow. The world can be good and pure only if our lives are, so let us purify ourselves.
items.core_idea: Purify yourself and the world follows.

items.plain: When we fail, we blame others. Nobody likes admitting their own faults and weaknesses; each of us tries to look blameless and pin it on someone or something else, even bad luck.
items.core_idea: In failure we blame others, not ourselves.

items.plain: The aim of all education should be making people grow, yet we keep polishing the outside. What use is polish when there is nothing inside?
items.core_idea: Education should build the person within.

items.plain: Like a bubble seen only when it bursts at the surface, we notice thoughts only once they are large or have become actions. If we could catch thought at its root, we could control everything.
items.core_idea: Control thought at its root to master yourself.
